note.title: Unearthed (Greenpeace UK), BP emails
note.text: Emails released under freedom of information show BP, which paid for the museum's Days of the Dead festival with the Mexican Embassy, asking for confirmation of Mexican government representation, and of UK government representation through DCMS, at the private evening of 30 October 2015, as it prepared to bid for drilling licences in the Gulf of Mexico. Bidding for Mexico's deepwater contracts began a month after the festival, and the embassy asked for the museum's guest list to be deleted after reading.

note.title: Culture Unstained dossier, via Hyperallergic
note.text: Emails in a Culture Unstained dossier show the museum's public affairs manager arranging a private meeting between Russia's ambassador, Alexander Yakovenko, two BP employees, director Hartwig Fischer and chair Richard Lambert on the morning of the Scythians press launch in May 2017, which the embassy called "very useful and positive". The show coincided with new US Senate sanctions on Russia, where BP holds a large stake in Rosneft; the sources do not say what was discussed.

note.title: Art Not Oil Coalition, FOI releases
note.text: Freedom of information releases to the Art Not Oil Coalition show BP's chief executive, Bob Dudley, inviting Culture Secretary John Whittingdale to the dinner the museum and BP gave for the opening of the Cosmonauts exhibition in 2015; he accepted and attended. A month after the May 2015 election BP's government affairs staff met Culture Minister Ed Vaizey, who welcomed BP's support for Cosmonauts, and the rest of the meeting notes was withheld as relating to the development of government policy.

note.title: Art Not Oil Coalition, FOI releases
note.text: BP invited the Culture Secretary to its Annual Business Reception at the British Museum on 12 November 2015, and Baroness Neville-Rolfe, a minister at the business department, called in, according to freedom of information releases to the Art Not Oil Coalition.

note.title: Art Not Oil Coalition, FOI releases
note.text: In February 2015 BP asked the gallery for at least 50 VIPs at the BP Portrait Award, with a breakdown that included government representatives, and in May a BP staff member proposed inviting Culture Minister Ed Vaizey to the award on 17 July, according to freedom of information releases to the Art Not Oil Coalition.

note.title: Philip Morris weekly update (Truth Tobacco Industry Documents)
note.text: A Philip Morris weekly update of 23 September 1994 says its cultural affairs director, Stephanie French, enlisted the Metropolitan Museum to call Council Speaker Peter Vallone and the Mayor's office against the Vallone anti-smoking bill, while Philip Morris was paying for the museum's Origins of Impressionism exhibition.

note.title: The New York Times, 26 September 1994 (Truth Tobacco Industry Documents)
note.text: The New York Times reported on 26 September 1994 that the academy, whose Next Wave Festival Philip Morris sponsored, made "discreet telephone calls" to City Council members about the Vallone anti-smoking bill after Philip Morris told it how it felt about the bill.

note.title: UK government hospitality return
note.text: A UK government hospitality return records BP giving Emily Walch, a special adviser at the business department, two tickets to a British Museum exhibition on 16 September 2014.

note.title: UK government hospitality return
note.text: A Cabinet Office hospitality return records its chief executive, John Manzoni, at the Royal Opera House on 10 June 2015 on tickets from Dev Sanyal of BP.

note.title: UK government hospitality returns
note.text: UK government hospitality returns record BP hosting Sue Owen, permanent secretary at the culture department, at the Portrait Award on 16 June 2015, and Sir Simon McDonald, head of the Foreign Office, at its Portrait Award reception on 11 June 2018.

note.title: UK government hospitality return
note.text: A culture department hospitality return records Bloomberg Philanthropies and the Serpentine hosting the arts minister, Lord Parkinson, at a reception on 19 April 2024.

note.title: UK government hospitality return
note.text: A government hospitality return records Bloomberg UK News hosting the Chief Whip, Jonathan Reynolds, at a drinks reception and private viewing of the collection at Tate Britain on 8 October 2025.
